text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The presidents of the three Baltic states want more clarity about the future security of their three states they said in a statement released on Saturday. They said they were still determined to join the alliance, which they see as the only way to ensure their security.
- Some 100 people protested against Lithuania's planned Butinge oil terminal, close to the Latvian border.
- The chairman of the Union of Christian Democrats and deputy Paul Klavinsh suffered a heart attack.
- The economic police will investigate all credits given out by the state privatisation fund.
- Drivers have to have their headlights switched on 24-hours a day from October 1.
- President Guntis Ulmanis explains his announcement on a moratorium on the death penalty.
- The state budget deficit was around 25 million lats on September 26.
- Russian and Latvian delegations will start talks today on the delimitation of their land border.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Friday said that he will seek the liquidation of two finance ministry posts, state revenue minister and state minister for investment and credit policy.
- Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans has promised to repair 500 kms of road next year.
- 35,000 cars were registered in Latvia since January 1.
